intent: Report the state of something that is not an action, as a small round dot with an optional label in the same tone.
typical_uses: A one-word state in a dense row or a table cell (running, failed, degraded)
A bare dot in a cell whose column header already names what it reports, named with aria-label

dont_use_when.situation: A status that needs a filled chip of its own, or sits alone as a column's whole content
A full-width note row in a conversation thread, with an icon, a border or a divider
A loading state with no settled value yet
A status mark pinned to the corner of an avatar
A clickable status that performs an action

invariants.text: With a `label` that renders something the root adds no role and no `aria-hidden`: the label is the announcement. Without one, the root is `aria-hidden="true"`, unless the caller passes `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, in which case the root takes `role="img"` instead so that name reaches the accessibility tree. `false`, `null`, `undefined` and `""` all count as no label. A `role` or `aria-hidden` the caller passes overrides either default, and the branches hold on whatever element `render` substitutes.

The tone class sets only `color` on the root; the dot fills from `currentColor` and the label inherits, so the two always share one tone. The resolved tone is reflected as `data-tone` on the root, and an explicit `tone={null}` resolves to neutral in both class and attribute.

`live` sets `data-live` on the root and breathes only the dot, on a 2s opacity cycle; the label keeps full opacity. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the animation is removed outright, not slowed, and `data-live` stays on the root.

anti_patterns.dont: Set a colour on the component from outside
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pick the `tone`; it owns the dot and the label together, in both themes

anti_patterns.dont: Keep `live` on a status that has settled
anti_patterns.do_instead: Drop `live` once the state is final - a moving dot beside "Completed" reads as unfinished work

anti_patterns.dont: Wrap it in a button or a link to make the status clickable
anti_patterns.do_instead: `render` is for the wrapping element only, such as an `li` in a status list

a11y.by: theme.css token contrast measured with src/__test-utils__/contrast.ts: the tone colour the label is painted in reaches 3.44:1 for light `success`, 1.96:1 for light `warning` and 4.29:1 for light `danger` against the light --background (success 3.77:1 and warning 2.15:1 on the white --card; light `danger` is 4.29:1 on --background but 4.70:1 on --card), under the 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 asks of the 12px label. A bare dot named with role="img" is a graphic under WCAG 1.4.11 and light `warning` misses its 3:1 as well. The accessible-name branches themselves hold: status-dot.test.tsx asserts aria-hidden="true" on a bare dot, role="img" with the caller's aria-label or aria-labelledby, and no role or aria-hidden once a label is shown, also under `render`.

label.states: label is a React node, not a string
label.because: `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (StatusDot passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the wrapping element, such as `render={<li />}` inside a status list.

unexposed_parts.reason: status-dot.tsx always renders it as the root's first child, painted from the tone; it is not exported as a component of its own, and the only controls over it are `tone` and `live`.
status-dot.tsx renders it only when `label` renders something; it is not exported as a component of its own, and what goes in it is the `label` prop.

good.title: A bare dot named for assistive tech
As a list item in a status list

bad.title: The label passed as children
bad.why: StatusDot's props omit `children`, so tsc refuses this; forced through, the caller's children are merged after the component's own and replace the dot and label spans, and with no `label` the root is still hidden from assistive tech. The text goes in `label`.

bad.title: A variant prop guessed from Badge
bad.why: StatusDot's paint axis is `tone`, not `variant`; the guessed prop is forwarded to the span and the dot stays neutral.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof statusDotVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The tone class-name builder StatusDot itself uses, exported beside the component.

label.description: Partially typed: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. label is a React node, not a string. `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (StatusDot passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the wrapping element, such as `render={<li />}` inside a status list.
